records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנֵּה֙ שָׁמַ֣עְתִּי בְקֹֽלְכֶ֔ם לְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־אֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם לִ֑י וָאַמְלִ֥יךְ עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם מֶֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And said Samuel to all Israel, behold, I have listened to your voice in all that you said to me, and I have made king over you a king.
pieces: Samuel said to all Israel, "I have listened to you and done everything you asked of me. I have set a king over you.

L.1: And Samuel said to all Israel, "Look, I have listened to your voice in everything that you said to me, and I have set a king over you.

R.1: Then Samuel spoke to all the people of Israel. He said, "I have done what you asked. I listened to you, and I have given you a king to rule over you.

decisions.choice: I have listened to your voice: Samuel did what the people asked in 8:5
decisions.reason: The words take up Yahweh's command to Samuel, "Listen to the voice of the people in all that they say to you" (8:7, 8:22). Samuel opens his farewell by saying that he has done exactly what he was told: the people asked for a king, and they have one.

decisions.choice: Samuel speaks at Gilgal, after Saul is made king there
decisions.reason: The chapter follows straight on from 11:14-15, where all the people went to Gilgal, made Saul king before Yahweh and offered peace offerings. Samuel's speech is his farewell as Israel's leader, and it opens a long speech that runs, with the people's answers, to the end of the chapter.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of verse 3
alternatives: one quotation from verse 1 to verse 25
decisions.reason: Samuel's first words run from verse 1 to verse 3; the people answer in verse 4, and the speech is taken up again in verse 5. Each part opens and closes its own quotation marks. Literal has "look" for the Hebrew pointing word; Balanced and Readable leave it out.

records.heading: Samuel calls Israel to witness his conduct

records.source: וְעַתָּ֞ה הִנֵּ֥ה הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ׀מִתְהַלֵּ֣ךְ לִפְנֵיכֶ֗ם וַאֲנִי֙ זָקַ֣נְתִּי וָשַׂ֔בְתִּי וּבָנַ֖י הִנָּ֣ם אִתְּכֶ֑ם וַאֲנִי֙ הִתְהַלַּ֣כְתִּי לִפְנֵיכֶ֔ם מִנְּעֻרַ֖י עַד־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And now behold, the king [is] walking before you, and I, I am old and gray, and my sons, behold, they [are] with you; and I, I have walked before you from my youth until this day.
pieces: Now the king will lead you. As for me, I am old and gray, and my sons are here among you. I have led you from my youth until this day.

L.2: And now, look, the king is walking before you, and I, I am old and gray, and my sons, look, they are with you; and I, I have walked before you from my youth until this day.

R.2: From now on the king will lead you. I am old now, and my hair is gray. My sons are here with you. I have been your leader ever since I was a young man.

decisions.choice: walk before you: lead you and live openly in your sight
decisions.reason: To walk before a people is to go ahead of them as their leader, in full view of them. The same words are used of the king and of Samuel: the king is now taking over the role Samuel has had all his life.

decisions.choice: I am old and gray, and my sons are with you
alternatives: my sons are with you: they are no longer in office, but ordinary members of the people
decisions.reason: The elders had given Samuel's age and his sons' failures as their reason for asking for a king (8:1-5). Samuel mentions his sons without defending them: they are there among the people, and anyone may bring a charge against them. He then turns to his own record.

decisions.choice: will lead you; I have led you (Balanced); will lead you; I have been your leader (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom "walk before". The Hebrew participle describes what is now under way, which English puts as "will lead you" from now on.

records.source: הִנְנִ֣י עֲנ֣וּ בִי֩ נֶ֨גֶד יְהוָ֜ה וְנֶ֣גֶד מְשִׁיח֗וֹ אֶת־שׁוֹר֩׀מִ֨י לָקַ֜חְתִּי וַחֲמ֧וֹר מִ֣י לָקַ֗חְתִּי וְאֶת־מִ֤י עָשַׁ֨קְתִּי֙ אֶת־מִ֣י רַצּ֔וֹתִי וּמִיַּד־מִי֙ לָקַ֣חְתִּי כֹ֔פֶר וְאַעְלִ֥ים עֵינַ֖י בּ֑וֹ וְאָשִׁ֖יב לָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Behold me, testify against me before YHWH and before his anointed: [the] ox of whom have I taken, and [the] donkey of whom have I taken, and whom have I oppressed, whom have I crushed, and from [the] hand of whom have I taken a ransom, and I hid my eyes with it? And I will restore [it] to you.
pieces: Here I am. Bring your charges against me before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointed. Whose ox did I take? Whose donkey? Whom did I cheat? Whom did I treat harshly? From whom did I take a bribe to make me look the other way? If I have, I will pay it back to you."

L.3: Here I am; testify against me before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointed: Whose ox have I taken, and whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I oppressed? Whom have I crushed? From whose hand have I taken a bribe to blind my eyes with it? And I will restore it to you."

R.3: Here I am. Tell me now, in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the king {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has anointed: Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey? Have I cheated anyone? Have I been cruel to anyone? Have I ever taken money from anyone to make me ignore what was wrong? If I have done any of these things, I will pay it back."

decisions.choice: his anointed: the king Yahweh has set apart, here Saul
decisions.reason: The anointed one is the person on whom oil was poured to set him apart for his office (10:1). Hannah's song already speaks of Yahweh's anointed king (2:10). Samuel calls on Yahweh and on the newly anointed king together as the witnesses of his record.

decisions.choice: ox, donkey, bribe: the abuses of a ruler
decisions.reason: Samuel names what a corrupt leader takes from the people. His questions answer his own warning about what a king would take (8:11-17) and the bribes his sons took (8:3). Moses made the same claim, that he had not taken one donkey from the people (Numbers 16:15).

decisions.choice: ransom here means a bribe
decisions.reason: The word means a payment that buys someone off. In a judge's hand it is a bribe paid to make him let a guilty person go (Amos 5:12).

decisions.choice: to hide my eyes with it: to look away from wrong
decisions.reason: A bribe blinds a judge's eyes so that he does not see the guilt in front of him (Exodus 23:8; Deuteronomy 16:19).

decisions.choice: to blind my eyes with it
alternatives: or even a pair of sandals (Greek)
decisions.reason: The Greek translation reads "a bribe, or even a pair of sandals? Testify against me" in place of "to blind my eyes with it", which seems to come from a Hebrew text differing by a few letters. The Hebrew text is followed here; the sense of the question is the same, that Samuel took no payment of any kind.

decisions.choice: the king he has anointed
decisions.reason: Readable spells out who the anointed one is, as the terms for Samuel set out for "the LORD's anointed".

decisions.choice: If I have, I will pay it back
decisions.reason: The Hebrew ends with a short "and I will restore it to you"; Balanced and Readable state the condition it implies.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ לֹ֥א עֲשַׁקְתָּ֖נוּ וְלֹ֣א רַצּוֹתָ֑נוּ וְלֹֽא־לָקַ֥חְתָּ מִיַּד־אִ֖ישׁ מְאֽוּמָה׃
records.gloss: And they said, not you have oppressed us and not you have crushed us, and not you have taken from [the] hand of anyone anything.
pieces: They answered, "You have not cheated us or treated us harshly, and you have not taken anything from anyone."

L.4: And they said, "You have not oppressed us, and you have not crushed us, and you have not taken anything from [the] hand of anyone."

R.4: The people answered, "No. You have never cheated us or been cruel to us. You have never taken anything from anyone."

decisions.choice: the people repeat Samuel's own words
decisions.reason: The people answer with the same verbs Samuel used (verse 3) and add "from anyone" and "anything" to make their answer complete. Samuel's record as a leader is cleared in full.

decisions.choice: cheated, treated harshly (Balanced); cheated, been cruel (Readable)
decisions.reason: The first verb means to oppress by taking what belongs to another, by force or fraud; the second means to crush, to treat someone roughly. Balanced and Readable use everyday words for both, as in verse 3.

decisions.choice: The people answered, "No.
decisions.reason: Readable names the speakers and adds "No" to make the answer clear.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם עֵ֧ד יְהוָ֣ה בָּכֶ֗ם וְעֵ֤ד מְשִׁיחוֹ֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֣י לֹ֧א מְצָאתֶ֛ם בְּיָדִ֖י מְא֑וּמָה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר עֵֽד׃פ
records.gloss: And he said to them, witness [is] YHWH against you, and witness [is] his anointed this day, that not you have found in my hand anything; and [one] said, witness.
pieces: Samuel said to them, "Today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is witness against you, and so is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointed: you have found nothing in my hand." "He is witness," they said.

L.5: And he said to them, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is witness against you, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointed is witness this day, that you have not found anything in my hand." And they said, "[He is] witness."

R.5: Samuel told them, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has heard you and is a witness against you, and so is the king {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has anointed. Today they have both heard you say that I have taken nothing from anyone." The people said, "Yes, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is witness."

decisions.choice: witness against you: the people are now bound by what they have said
decisions.reason: Yahweh and the king are witnesses "against" the people: if the people later complain about Samuel, these witnesses will stand against their complaint. Samuel's record is settled before the king takes over.

decisions.choice: and they said (the sense of the singular verb)
alternatives: and he said: one man answered for the people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is singular, "and he said": either the people answer as one, or one person speaks for them all. Some Hebrew manuscripts and the Greek and Syriac translations have the plural "they said". The meaning is the same either way: the people agree.

decisions.choice: found in my hand: found that I have taken
decisions.reason: What is "in my hand" is what I hold or have taken. The people have found that Samuel took nothing that was not his.

decisions.choice: [He is] witness
decisions.reason: The people answer with one word, "Witness". Literal supplies "he is"; Balanced writes it without brackets; Readable names Yahweh as the witness, since the reply takes up Samuel's first words.

decisions.choice: they have both heard you say that I have taken nothing from anyone
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what the witnesses are witnesses to.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל אֶל־הָעָ֑ם יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשָׂה֙ אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאֶֽת־אַהֲרֹ֔ן וַאֲשֶׁ֧ר הֶעֱלָ֛ה אֶת־אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And said Samuel to the people, YHWH, who made Moses and Aaron, and who brought up your fathers from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: Samuel said to the people, "It is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who appointed Moses and Aaron and brought your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} up from the land of Egypt.

L.6: And Samuel said to the people, "[It is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who made Moses and Aaron, and who brought your fathers up from the land of Egypt.

R.6: Then Samuel said to the people, "It was {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders. He brought your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} up out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew has "Yahweh, who made Moses and Aaron" with no verb
alternatives: Yahweh is witness, who appointed Moses and Aaron (Greek)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence names Yahweh and says what he has done, but has no main verb. The Greek translation adds "is witness", taking up verse 5: "Yahweh is witness, who made Moses and Aaron". The Hebrew text is followed here and read as a statement that it is Yahweh who did these things; verse 7 goes on to the case Samuel makes from them.

decisions.choice: made: appointed to their task
decisions.reason: The verb "make" is used here of putting people into an office, as it is of priests (1 Kings 12:31). Yahweh did not only send Moses and Aaron; he made them the leaders they were.

decisions.choice: It is (It was) the LORD who ...
decisions.reason: English needs a verb. Literal brackets "It is"; Balanced and Readable write it plainly. Readable says what "appointed" meant for Moses and Aaron: to lead the people.

decisions.choice: appointed (Balanced); chose ... to be your leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "made" here; Literal keeps the Hebrew word.

records.heading: Samuel recalls what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִֽתְיַצְּב֛וּ וְאִשָּׁפְטָ֥ה אִתְּכֶ֖ם לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אֵ֚ת כָּל־צִדְק֣וֹת יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה אִתְּכֶ֖ם וְאֶת־אֲבוֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And now, present yourselves, and I will enter into judgment with you before YHWH [concerning] all [the] righteous acts of YHWH which he did with you and with your fathers.
pieces: So now take your stand, and I will put the case to you before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, recounting all the righteous acts that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done for you and for your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}.

L.7: And now, present yourselves, and let me enter into judgment with you before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [concerning] all the righteous acts of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did with you and with your fathers.

R.7: Now stand here in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I am going to argue my case with you. I will remind you of all the good and right things {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done to save you and your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}.

decisions.choice: take your stand ... enter into judgment: Samuel speaks like a man making a case in court
decisions.reason: The people are to stand as at a hearing, and Samuel will argue a case with them before Yahweh as judge. The same picture of a lawsuit between Yahweh and his people is used by the prophets (Micah 6:1-5; Jeremiah 2:9).

decisions.choice: righteous acts: the deeds by which Yahweh rescued his people and kept faith with them
decisions.reason: The plural of the word for righteousness names Yahweh's saving deeds, the acts in which he did right by his people and set them free. The Song of Deborah uses the same phrase for the victories of Yahweh (Judges 5:11). Samuel's list follows in verses 8-11.

decisions.choice: recounting
decisions.reason: The Hebrew simply puts "all the righteous acts" after the verb as the matter of the case. Literal supplies [concerning]; Balanced adds "recounting" to show how the righteous acts belong to the case.

decisions.choice: the good and right things the LORD has done to save you
decisions.reason: Readable explains "righteous acts": what the LORD did to rescue the people, which showed that he was right and faithful.

records.source: כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥א יַעֲקֹ֖ב מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיִּזְעֲק֤וּ אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאֶֽת־אַהֲרֹ֗ן וַיּוֹצִ֤יאוּ אֶת־אֲבֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וַיֹּשִׁב֖וּם בַּמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: When went Jacob [to] Egypt, and cried out your fathers to YHWH, and sent YHWH Moses and Aaron, and they brought out your fathers from Egypt, and they settled them in this place.
pieces: After Jacob went to Egypt, your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} out of Egypt and settled them in this place.

L.8: When Jacob went to Egypt, your fathers cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent Moses and Aaron, and they brought your fathers out of Egypt and settled them in this place.

R.8: Long ago Jacob and his family went down to Egypt. Later your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent Moses and Aaron. They led your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} out of Egypt and gave them a home in this land.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew moves straight from Jacob's going to Egypt to the cry
alternatives: and the Egyptians humbled them, and your fathers cried out (Greek)
decisions.reason: The Greek translation adds "and the Egyptians oppressed them" before "your fathers cried out". The Hebrew leaves the oppression to be understood from the story of Exodus 1-3. The sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: cried out ... sent: the pattern of the exodus
decisions.reason: Israel cried out and Yahweh heard (Exodus 2:23-25; 3:7-10). Samuel's history follows a repeated pattern: the people cry out, Yahweh sends a deliverer (verses 8, 10-11).

decisions.choice: they brought out ... and they settled them: Moses and Aaron as Yahweh's agents
decisions.reason: Both verbs are plural, so their subject is Moses and Aaron. Moses and Aaron did not themselves lead the people into the land; Samuel tells the whole rescue as the work Yahweh did through the leaders he sent. The Greek translation has "he settled them", with Yahweh as subject.

decisions.choice: Long ago Jacob and his family went down to Egypt. Later ... for help
decisions.reason: Readable explains that Jacob went with his family (Genesis 46), and that the cry came later and was a cry for help.

records.source: וַֽיִּשְׁכְּח֖וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּמְכֹּ֣ר אֹתָ֡ם בְּיַ֣ד סִֽיסְרָא֩ שַׂר־צְבָ֨א חָצ֜וֹר וּבְיַד־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וּבְיַד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֔ב וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ בָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And they forgot YHWH their God, and he sold them into [the] hand of Sisera, commander of [the] army of Hazor, and into [the] hand of [the] Philistines, and into [the] hand of [the] king of Moab, and they fought against them.
pieces: But they forgot {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sold them into the power of Sisera, who was commander of the army of Hazor, and into the power of the Philistines and the king of Moab, and these fought against them.

L.9: And they forgot {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sold them into [the] hand of Sisera, the commander of the army of Hazor, and into [the] hand of the Philistines, and into [the] hand of the king of Moab, and they fought against them.

R.9: But your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} forgot {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} handed them over to Sisera, the army commander from the city of Hazor. He also handed them over to the Philistines and to the king of Moab. All these enemies made war on them.

decisions.choice: forgot: left Yahweh out of their lives and loyalty
decisions.reason: To forget Yahweh is not a lapse of memory but a turning away from him to other gods, as verse 10 confesses (Judges 3:7; Deuteronomy 8:19).

decisions.choice: sold them into the hand of: gave them over to the power of
decisions.reason: As in Judges (2:14; 3:8; 4:2), Yahweh "sells" his people to their enemies: he lets them fall under foreign power, as a master hands over what is his.

decisions.choice: Sisera, the Philistines, the king of Moab: oppressors from the book of Judges
decisions.reason: Sisera commanded the army of Jabin king of Hazor (Judges 4:2); the king of Moab is Eglon (Judges 3:12-14); the Philistines oppressed Israel in the days of Samson and later (Judges 10:7; 13:1). Samuel does not list them in the order of Judges.

decisions.choice: sold them into [the] hand of (Literal); sold them into the power of (Balanced); handed them over to (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording follows the one used throughout Judges for this phrase.

decisions.choice: the city of Hazor
decisions.reason: Readable adds that Hazor was a city, so that the reader does not take it for a person.

records.source: וַיִּזְעֲק֤וּ אֶל־יְהוָה֙ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּחָטָ֔אנוּ כִּ֤י עָזַ֨בְנוּ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה וַנַּעֲבֹ֥ד אֶת־הַבְּעָלִ֖ים וְאֶת־הָעַשְׁתָּר֑וֹת וְעַתָּ֗ה הַצִּילֵ֛נוּ מִיַּ֥ד אֹיְבֵ֖ינוּ וְנַעַבְדֶֽךָּ׃
records.gloss: And they cried out to YHWH and said, we have sinned, for we have forsaken YHWH and we have served the Baals and the Ashtaroth; and now deliver us from [the] hand of our enemies, and we will serve you.
pieces: Then they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, 'We have sinned. We have abandoned {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and served the Baals and the Ashtaroth. But now rescue us from the power of our enemies, and we will serve {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'

L.10: And they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, 'We have sinned, because we have forsaken {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and have served the Baals and the Ashtaroth; and now deliver us from [the] hand of our enemies, and we will serve {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'

R.10: Then they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They said, 'We have sinned. We turned away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and worshiped the false gods called the Baals and the goddesses called the Ashtaroth. But now save us from our enemies, and we will worship {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'

decisions.choice: and they said: the reading spoken aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has "and he said", singular; the reading marked for reading aloud has the plural "and they said", which fits "they cried out". The plural is followed here. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the Baals and the Ashtaroth: the gods and goddesses of Canaan
decisions.reason: Baal was the Canaanite storm god and Ashtoreth (Astarte) a goddess of fertility and war. The plurals cover their many local forms. Samuel had called on Israel to put them away (7:3-4).

decisions.choice: We have sinned ... deliver us, and we will serve you
decisions.reason: The words are close to Israel's confession in Judges 10:10-16. Samuel lets the ancestors' own prayer show that serving Yahweh, not having a king, was the way out of oppression.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for the ancestors' words
decisions.reason: The people's prayer is quoted inside Samuel's speech, so it takes single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: the false gods called the Baals and the goddesses called the Ashtaroth
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the Baals and the Ashtaroth were, as in Judges 2:13.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ אֶת־יְרֻבַּ֣עַל וְאֶת־בְּדָ֔ן וְאֶת־יִפְתָּ֖ח וְאֶת־שְׁמוּאֵ֑ל וַיַּצֵּ֨ל אֶתְכֶ֜ם מִיַּ֤ד אֹֽיְבֵיכֶם֙ מִסָּבִ֔יב וַתֵּשְׁב֖וּ בֶּֽטַח׃
records.gloss: And sent YHWH Jerubbaal and Bedan and Jephthah and Samuel, and he delivered you from [the] hand of your enemies around, and you dwelt [in] security.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah and Samuel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescued you from the power of the enemies around you, and you lived in safety.

L.11: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent Jerubbaal and Bedan and Jephthah and Samuel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} delivered you from [the] hand of your enemies all around, and you dwelt in security.

R.11: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent Jerubbaal (also called Gideon), Bedan, Jephthah and Samuel. He used them to save you from the enemies all around you, and you lived in safety.

decisions.choice: Bedan
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has Bedan, a name not found among the judges in the book of Judges (a Bedan of the tribe of Manasseh is named in 1 Chronicles 7:17). The Greek and Syriac translations read "Barak", the leader who fought Sisera with Deborah (Judges 4), which fits the mention of Sisera in verse 9. Bedan may be another name for a known judge, or the text may have changed in copying. The Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: Samuel
decisions.reason: Samuel names himself last among the deliverers, as the one who led Israel against the Philistines (7:7-14). Some Greek manuscripts and the Syriac translation read "Samson" instead, which avoids Samuel speaking of himself in the third person. The Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: Jerubbaal is Gideon
decisions.reason: Gideon was given the name Jerubbaal, "let Baal contend", after he tore down Baal's altar (Judges 6:32).

decisions.choice: he delivered you: Yahweh is the rescuer
decisions.reason: The leaders are sent, but the one who delivers is Yahweh; the verb is singular and its subject is Yahweh. This prepares for verse 12: Israel already had a king who rescued them.

decisions.choice: (also called Gideon)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the better known name, so that the reader recognizes the judge.

decisions.choice: He used them to save you
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the LORD saved the people through the leaders he sent.

records.source: וַתִּרְא֗וּ כִּֽי־נָחָ֞שׁ מֶ֣לֶךְ בְּנֵֽי־עַמּוֹן֮ בָּ֣א עֲלֵיכֶם֒ וַתֹּ֣אמְרוּ לִ֔י לֹ֕א כִּי־מֶ֖לֶךְ יִמְלֹ֣ךְ עָלֵ֑ינוּ וַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם מַלְכְּכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you saw that Nahash king of [the] sons of Ammon came against you, and you said to me, no, but a king shall reign over us; and YHWH your God [was] your king.
pieces: But when you saw that Nahash king of the Ammonites was coming against you, you said to me, 'No! A king must reign over us,' though {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God was your king.

L.12: And when you saw that Nahash, the king of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ammon, came against you, you said to me, 'No, but a king shall reign over us,' when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God was your king.

R.12: But when you saw that Nahash, the king of the Ammonites, was coming to attack you, you told me, 'No! We want a king to rule over us.' You said this even though {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God was already your king.

decisions.choice: Nahash: the Ammonite king of chapter 11
decisions.reason: Nahash besieged Jabesh-gilead and was defeated by Saul (11:1-11). Samuel ties the people's demand for a king to their fear of him, though the request itself is first told in 8:4-5; the threat from Ammon may already have been growing then.

decisions.choice: No, but a king shall reign over us
decisions.reason: The people's words echo their answer in 8:19, "No, but there shall be a king over us". Samuel quotes them back to show what they rejected.

decisions.choice: Yahweh your God was your king
decisions.reason: The heart of Samuel's charge: Israel already had a king, Yahweh, who had rescued them again and again (verses 8-11). Asking for a human king was a rejection of him (8:7; 10:19).

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for the people's earlier words
decisions.reason: Samuel quotes what the people said to him, inside his own speech.

decisions.choice: the Ammonites
decisions.reason: "Sons of Ammon" is the name of the people; Balanced and Readable call them the Ammonites.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִנֵּ֥ה הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּחַרְתֶּ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר שְׁאֶלְתֶּ֑ם וְהִנֵּ֨ה נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם מֶֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And now, behold, the king whom you have chosen, whom you asked for; and behold, has set YHWH over you a king.
pieces: Now here is the king you have chosen, the one you asked for. See, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has set a king over you.

L.13: And now, here [is] the king whom you have chosen, whom you have asked for; and look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has set a king over you.

R.13: So here is the king you chose. You asked for him, and now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given you a king to rule over you.

decisions.choice: whom you asked for: a play on Saul's name
decisions.reason: The verb "ask" has the same letters as the name Saul, which means "asked for". The people asked for a king (8:10), and the king they were given is Saul, the "asked-for" one. The same verb returns in verses 17 and 19, where asking for a king is called evil.

decisions.choice: you have chosen ... Yahweh has set: both are true
decisions.reason: The king is the people's choice, made at their own request, and yet it is Yahweh who has given him (10:24). Samuel holds the two side by side: Yahweh granted what the people wanted, and both the people and their king now answer to him (verses 14-15).

decisions.choice: here [is] ... look (Literal); here is ... See (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The two pointing words direct the eye to the king and to Yahweh's act. Literal has "here [is]" and "look"; Balanced uses "here is" and "see"; Readable leaves them out.

records.source: אִם־תִּֽירְא֣וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֗ה וַעֲבַדְתֶּ֤ם אֹתוֹ֙ וּשְׁמַעְתֶּ֣ם בְּקֹל֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א תַמְר֖וּ אֶת־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וִהְיִתֶ֣ם גַּם־אַתֶּ֗ם וְגַם־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָלַ֣ךְ עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם אַחַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: If you will fear YHWH and serve him and listen to his voice and not rebel against [the] mouth of YHWH, and will be both you and also the king who reigns over you after YHWH your God.
pieces: If you fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice and do not rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command, then both you and the king who reigns over you will be followers of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.14: If you fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and listen to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice and do not rebel against the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, then both you and the king who reigns over you will be after {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.14: If you respect {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, if you obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and do not refuse to do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commands, then you and the king who rules over you will keep following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: then both you and the king ... will be after Yahweh your God
alternatives: if ... and if both you and the king who reigns over you follow Yahweh your God, [it will be well]
decisions.reason: The sentence begins with "if", and verse 15 has an "if" with a clear "then" ("the hand of Yahweh will be against you"). Here the "then" is less clear. It is taken to be the last clause: if the people are loyal, they and their king will go on following Yahweh as his people. Others read the last clause as part of the "if" and take the sentence as broken off, leaving the reader to supply "it will be well". The Greek translation does not settle it.

decisions.choice: fear Yahweh: hold him in awe and be loyal to him
decisions.reason: To fear Yahweh is to honor him as God and to live in obedience to him. The verbs that follow (serve, listen, not rebel) spell out what it means.

decisions.choice: rebel against the mouth of Yahweh: refuse what Yahweh commands
decisions.reason: The mouth stands for what Yahweh says, his command (Numbers 20:24; Deuteronomy 1:26, 43).

decisions.choice: be after Yahweh: follow him as his loyal people
decisions.reason: To be or go "after" someone is to follow him as leader and to be on his side (2 Samuel 2:10; 1 Kings 14:8).

decisions.choice: the LORD's command; followers of (Balanced); what the LORD commands; keep following (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "mouth" and of "be after". Readable repeats "if" to make the long condition easier to follow.

decisions.choice: respect ... worship
decisions.reason: Readable says "respect" for "fear" and "worship" for "serve", the sense these words have when used of God.

records.source: וְאִם־לֹ֤א תִשְׁמְעוּ֙ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֔ה וּמְרִיתֶ֖ם אֶת־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְהָיְתָ֧ה יַד־יְהוָ֛ה בָּכֶ֖ם וּבַאֲבֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And if not you will listen to [the] voice of YHWH and you rebel against [the] mouth of YHWH, and will be [the] hand of YHWH against you and against your fathers.
pieces: But if you do not obey the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and you rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command, then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s hand will be against you, as it was against your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}.

L.15: But if you do not listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and you rebel against the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, then the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be against you and against your fathers.

R.15: But if you refuse to obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and refuse to do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commands, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will punish you, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} punished your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}.

decisions.choice: against you and against your fathers: as it was against your fathers
alternatives: against you and against your king (Greek)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "against you and against your fathers", which is hard, since the fathers are long dead. It is taken to mean that Yahweh's hand will be against the people as it was against their fathers (verse 9). The Greek translation reads "against you and against your king", which matches verse 14 and verse 25.

decisions.choice: the hand of Yahweh will be against you: Yahweh will act against you to punish
decisions.reason: Yahweh's hand is his power in action. Against an enemy it strikes (5:6, 9; 7:13); here it is turned against his own people if they rebel.

decisions.choice: as it was against your ancestors (Balanced); just as he punished your ancestors (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense taken in the meaning decision. Literal keeps the Hebrew as it stands.

decisions.choice: will punish you
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the picture of Yahweh's hand against someone.

records.source: גַּם־עַתָּה֙ הִתְיַצְּב֣וּ וּרְא֔וּ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַגָּד֖וֹל הַזֶּ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה עֹשֶׂ֖ה לְעֵינֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Also now present yourselves and see this great thing which YHWH [is] doing before your eyes.
pieces: Now then, take your stand and watch this great thing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is about to do before your eyes.

L.16: Even now, present yourselves and see this great thing which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is about to do before your eyes.

R.16: Now stay where you are and watch the amazing thing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is going to do right in front of you.

decisions.choice: present yourselves and see: the words of Moses at the Red Sea
decisions.reason: Moses told the people, "Stand firm and see the salvation of Yahweh" (Exodus 14:13). Samuel uses the same verbs for a sign that will show Yahweh's power again, this time against the people's sin.

decisions.choice: is about to do: the participle points to something just ahead
decisions.reason: The verb form describes an action that is about to happen. The sign comes in verse 18, after Samuel calls on Yahweh.

decisions.choice: present yourselves (Literal); take your stand (Balanced); stay where you are (Readable)
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 7. Balanced keeps the courtroom picture of standing for a hearing; Readable says it simply.

records.source: הֲל֤וֹא קְצִיר־חִטִּים֙ הַיּ֔וֹם אֶקְרָא֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וְיִתֵּ֥ן קֹל֖וֹת וּמָטָ֑ר וּדְע֣וּ וּרְא֗וּ כִּֽי־רָעַתְכֶ֤ם רַבָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר עֲשִׂיתֶם֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לִשְׁא֥וֹל לָכֶ֖ם מֶֽלֶךְ׃ס
records.gloss: [Is it] not [the] harvest of wheat today? I will call to YHWH and he will give voices and rain, and know and see that your evil [is] great which you did in [the] eyes of YHWH, to ask for yourselves a king.
pieces: Is this not the time of the wheat harvest? I will call on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send thunder and rain. Then you will know and see how great is the evil you have done in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by asking for a king for yourselves."

L.17: Is it not wheat harvest today? I will call to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give thunder and rain; and know and see that your evil is great which you have done in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by asking for yourselves a king."

R.17: It is the time of the wheat harvest now, when it does not rain. But I will pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send thunder and rain. Then you will understand how wicked it was in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for you to ask for a king."

decisions.choice: wheat harvest: early summer, in the dry season
decisions.reason: In Israel wheat is harvested in late spring and early summer, when rain almost never falls. A storm at that time would be a plain sign from Yahweh, and could also ruin the crop that was waiting to be gathered.

decisions.choice: voices: thunder
decisions.reason: The plural of the word for "voice" is the regular word for thunder, heard as the voice of God (Exodus 9:23; Psalm 29:3).

decisions.choice: know and see: the purpose of the sign
decisions.reason: The two commands follow the promise of the sign and state its purpose: when the storm comes, the people are to recognize their wrong.

decisions.choice: your evil is great ... by asking for yourselves a king
decisions.reason: Samuel does not say that kingship itself is evil; Yahweh has given the king (verse 13). The evil was asking for a king in place of Yahweh as king (verse 12; 8:7).

decisions.choice: send thunder and rain
decisions.reason: "Give voices" is the Hebrew way of saying that God sends thunder. Literal keeps "give"; Balanced and Readable say "send".

decisions.choice: It is the time of the wheat harvest now, when it does not rain. But
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a statement and says why the season matters, so that the sign is clear to a reader who does not know the climate of Israel.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה קֹלֹ֥ת וּמָטָ֖ר בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַיִּירָ֨א כָל־הָעָ֥ם מְאֹ֛ד אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת־שְׁמוּאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And called Samuel to YHWH, and gave YHWH voices and rain on the day that, and feared all the people greatly YHWH and Samuel.
pieces: So Samuel called on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and that same day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent thunder and rain. All the people were filled with fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and of Samuel.

L.18: And Samuel called to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave thunder and rain on that day; and all the people greatly feared {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and Samuel.

R.18: So Samuel prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and that same day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent thunder and rain. Then all the people were very afraid of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and of Samuel.

decisions.choice: feared: awe and terror together
decisions.reason: The people fear Yahweh in the sense of verse 14, honoring him, and they are also afraid of what he may do to them, as verse 19 shows. Samuel is feared too, because Yahweh has answered his prayer.

decisions.choice: feared Yahweh and Samuel: as Israel feared Yahweh and Moses
decisions.reason: After the crossing of the sea, the people "feared Yahweh and believed in Yahweh and in Moses his servant" (Exodus 14:31). Samuel is shown as a prophet like Moses.

decisions.choice: were filled with fear of (Balanced); were very afraid of (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable choose words that hold both awe and fright.

records.heading: Thunder and rain at harvest time

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ כָל־הָעָ֜ם אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל הִתְפַּלֵּ֧ל בְּעַד־עֲבָדֶ֛יךָ אֶל־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ וְאַל־נָמ֑וּת כִּֽי־יָסַ֤פְנוּ עַל־כָּל־חַטֹּאתֵ֨ינוּ֙ רָעָ֔ה לִשְׁאֹ֥ל לָ֖נוּ מֶֽלֶךְ׃ס
records.gloss: And said all the people to Samuel, pray for your slaves to YHWH your God, and not let us die, for we have added to all our sins evil, to ask for ourselves a king.
pieces: All the people said to Samuel, "Pray for your servants to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, or we will die! To all our other sins we have added this evil: we asked for a king for ourselves."

L.19: And all the people said to Samuel, "Pray for your servants to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, so that we do not die, for we have added to all our sins an evil, by asking for ourselves a king."

R.19: All the people begged Samuel, "Please pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God for us, your servants, so that we will not die. We have sinned in many ways, and now we have added one more evil thing: we asked for a king."

decisions.choice: your servants: a humble way of speaking of oneself
decisions.reason: Speaking to someone of higher standing, a person called himself "your slave" as a mark of respect and dependence. The people place themselves under Samuel as they ask him to pray for them.

decisions.choice: pray for your servants: Samuel stands between the people and Yahweh
decisions.reason: The people ask Samuel to intercede, as Israel asked Moses (Numbers 21:7). Samuel answers in verse 23 that he will not stop praying for them.

decisions.choice: Yahweh your God: said to Samuel
decisions.reason: The people speak of "your God" to Samuel, as one who stands close to Yahweh. In their fear they turn to Samuel as the one Yahweh hears. Samuel answers that Yahweh will not abandon "his people" (verse 22).

decisions.choice: your servants (every level)
decisions.reason: The people are not literally owned; this is the polite way of speaking of oneself, which has "your servant(s)" at every level in these books.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֤ל אֶל־הָעָם֙ אַל־תִּירָ֔אוּ אַתֶּ֣ם עֲשִׂיתֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את אַ֗ךְ אַל־תָּס֨וּרוּ֙ מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַעֲבַדְתֶּ֥ם אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה בְּכָל־לְבַבְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And said Samuel to the people, not be afraid; you, you have done all this evil; only not turn aside from after YHWH, and serve YHWH with all your heart.
pieces: Samuel said to the people, "Do not be afraid. You have done all this evil, yes; but do not turn away from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all your heart.

L.20: And Samuel said to the people, "Do not be afraid. You, you have done all this evil; only do not turn aside from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all your heart.

R.20: Samuel answered the people, "Do not be afraid. It is true that you have done this evil thing. But do not stop following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with your whole heart.

decisions.choice: you, you have done: the pronoun stressed
decisions.reason: Samuel does not deny the people's guilt; the stated "you" admits it fully. The turn comes with "only": guilt is no reason to give up on Yahweh.

decisions.choice: turn aside from after Yahweh: stop following him
decisions.reason: To walk "after" Yahweh is to follow him; to turn aside from after him is to leave his way for other gods (Deuteronomy 11:16, 28).

decisions.choice: serve Yahweh with all your heart
decisions.reason: The words recall the commands of Deuteronomy to love and serve Yahweh with all the heart (Deuteronomy 10:12; 11:13). Samuel called for the same in 7:3.

decisions.choice: Samuel's speech opens here and closes at the end of verse 25
decisions.reason: Samuel's second speech runs to the end of the chapter, so the quotation opens here and closes in verse 25.

records.source: וְלֹ֖א תָּס֑וּרוּ כִּ֣י׀אַחֲרֵ֣י הַתֹּ֗הוּ אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־יוֹעִ֛ילוּ וְלֹ֥א יַצִּ֖ילוּ כִּי־תֹ֥הוּ הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: And not you shall turn aside, for after the emptiness which not profit and not deliver, for emptiness they [are].
pieces: Do not turn aside to follow worthless things that cannot help you or rescue you, because they are worthless.

L.21: And do not turn aside, for [then you would go] after empty things which cannot profit and cannot deliver, for they are emptiness.

R.21: Do not turn away to follow idols. They are useless. They cannot help you or save you, because they are nothing at all.

decisions.choice: emptiness: false gods
decisions.reason: The word means something formless and empty, a waste (Genesis 1:2; Isaiah 45:18). Here it names the idols Israel might follow: they are nothing, and they can do nothing (Isaiah 41:29; 44:9).

decisions.choice: for after emptiness: a short way of saying where turning aside would lead
alternatives: do not turn aside after empty things (Greek)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is clipped: "do not turn aside, for after emptiness". The sense is that turning away from Yahweh means going after empty gods. The Greek translation leaves out "for", reading "do not turn aside after the empty things". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: cannot profit and cannot deliver
decisions.reason: Samuel sets the idols against Yahweh, who delivered Israel again and again (verses 10-11). The people asked for deliverance; only Yahweh can give it.

decisions.choice: [then you would go]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the words needed to make the clipped Hebrew read in English.

decisions.choice: idols ... nothing at all
decisions.reason: Readable names what the empty things are and gives the sense of "emptiness".

records.gloss: For not will abandon YHWH his people for the sake of his name the great, for has been pleased YHWH to make you for himself a people.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great name's sake {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not forsake {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has been pleased to make you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people.

L.22: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not abandon {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great name, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has been pleased to make you a people for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.

R.22: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will not leave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. He will keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great name honored. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was glad to make you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people.

decisions.choice: for the sake of his great name: Yahweh's own honor is at stake
decisions.reason: Yahweh's name is his known character and reputation among the nations. If he abandoned his people, it would be said that he could not keep them (Joshua 7:9; Numbers 14:15-16). His faithfulness does not rest on Israel's goodness.

decisions.choice: has been pleased: chose freely and willingly
decisions.reason: The verb means to decide or to be willing to do something. Yahweh chose Israel by his own free will, as Deuteronomy 7:7-8 says.

decisions.choice: to make you a people for himself
decisions.reason: This takes up the covenant promise, "I will take you as my people" (Exodus 6:7; Deuteronomy 29:12).

decisions.choice: He will keep his great name honored
decisions.reason: Readable explains what acting "for the sake of his name" means: protecting his honor and reputation.

records.source: גַּ֣ם אָנֹכִ֗י חָלִ֤ילָה לִּי֙ מֵחֲטֹ֣א לַֽיהוָ֔ה מֵחֲדֹ֖ל לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל בַּעַדְכֶ֑ם וְהוֹרֵיתִ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ הַטּוֹבָ֖ה וְהַיְשָׁרָֽה׃
records.gloss: Also I, far be it to me from sinning against YHWH from ceasing to pray for you; and I will teach you in [the] way, the good and the upright.
pieces: As for me, far be it from me to sin against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by ceasing to pray for you. I will go on teaching you the way that is good and right.

L.23: As for me also, far be it from me to sin against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by ceasing to pray for you; and I will teach you the good and upright way.

R.23: As for me, I will never sin against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by stopping my prayers for you. I will keep on teaching you to live in a way that is good and right.

decisions.choice: far be it from me: a strong refusal
decisions.reason: The expression is an oath-like refusal: "May it never be that I do this!" (Genesis 18:25; Joshua 24:16).

decisions.choice: to stop praying for the people would be a sin against Yahweh
decisions.reason: Samuel treats prayer for the people as part of the task Yahweh gave him. Though he is no longer their leader in battle and law, he remains their prophet who prays and teaches (7:5, 8-9).

decisions.choice: teach you the way: instruct you how to live
decisions.reason: The way is a path of life. The verb for "teach" is related to the word for instruction or law; Samuel will go on showing the people how Yahweh wants them to live.

decisions.choice: go on teaching (Balanced); keep on teaching (Readable)
decisions.reason: Samuel has always taught the people; Balanced and Readable show that this goes on, set beside his ceasing to pray, which he refuses.

records.gloss: Only fear YHWH and serve him in truth with all your heart; for see what he has done great with you.
pieces: Only fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} faithfully with all your heart. Think of the great things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done for you.

L.24: Only fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in truth with all your heart; for see what great things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done for you.

R.24: Just respect {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} faithfully with your whole heart. Remember the great things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done for you.

decisions.choice: in truth: faithfully, with loyalty
decisions.reason: The word means firmness and faithfulness, and so truth. To serve "in truth" is to serve with steady loyalty, not with a show of worship (Joshua 24:14).

decisions.choice: for see what great things he has done: the reason to serve
alternatives: see the great thing he has done (the storm)
decisions.reason: The "for" gives the reason for the command: Yahweh's great acts, including the sign just given (verse 18) and the history of verses 8-11, call for faithful service.

decisions.choice: faithfully; Think of (Balanced); Remember (Readable)
decisions.reason: "See" here means to consider. Balanced and Readable give that sense, and "faithfully" for "in truth".

records.gloss: And if doing evil you do evil, both you and your king will be swept away.
pieces: But if you go on doing evil, you and your king alike will be swept away."

L.25: But if you indeed do evil, both you and your king will be swept away."

R.25: But if you keep on doing evil, both you and your king will be destroyed."

decisions.choice: doing evil you do evil: going on in evil
alternatives: if you do evil at all
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. It describes a settled course of evil, not a single wrong.

decisions.choice: swept away: destroyed, as by a sudden end
decisions.reason: The verb is used of being carried off and destroyed (Genesis 19:15, 17). The warning comes true for Saul (31:1-6), and in the end for the kingdom when it is taken into exile.

decisions.choice: indeed do evil (Literal); go on doing evil (Balanced); keep on doing evil (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level gives the force of the doubled verb in its own way. The quotation that opened in verse 20 closes here.
